prompt: A segment tree node stores only the named aggregate of its range, combined from the same aggregates in its two children. Assume unit-cost arithmetic and no growing sets or sorted lists as summaries. Which range queries can a plain (non-lazy) segment tree answer in O(log n) with point updates, where n is the array length? Select all that apply.

options.explanation: Correct. gcd is associative, with identity 0, so ranges combine from halves.

options.text: Ordered product of the range’s two-by-two matrices
options.explanation: Correct. Matrix multiplication is associative but not commutative. That is fine as long as the left child is always combined before the right.
The median of two halves cannot be computed from their medians alone; it is not a decomposable summary, so a plain segment tree cannot do it.
Two halves with 3 distinct values each could have 3 to 6 together; the counts do not combine. This needs offline tricks or persistent trees.
Correct. max is associative with identity −infinity.

workedExample: Ask whether the two child summaries determine the parent summary. Child gcds, ordered matrix products and maxima do, with associative combines. Two medians do not describe the relative ordering of all values; two distinct counts do not describe which values overlap. Fixed-size matrices and the stated arithmetic model keep each combine constant-cost. Preserve left-to-right order for matrix multiplication.

prompt: A maximum-subarray tree stores each child’s best interior subarray. Why must it also store prefix and suffix summaries?

options.text: A best subarray must always include the parent’s entire range.
options.explanation: It may lie wholly inside one child or cross the split.

options.text: Prefix and suffix summaries make every child sum positive.
options.explanation: Summaries report actual values and cannot change signs.

options.text: The parent’s best subarray may cross the split, joining a left suffix to a right prefix.
options.explanation: Correct. Child interior bests alone miss this third case.

options.text: They let the tree reorder elements before combining.
options.explanation: Subarrays depend on the original order; reordering would change the question.

workedExample: A candidate either stays entirely in the left child, stays entirely in the right child, or crosses the split. A crossing contiguous subarray must end with a suffix of the left child and begin with a prefix of the right. Those summaries retain exactly the missing information.
